[P2] Distinguish clock resets from main-thread stalls

A regression exceeding one second does not necessarily indicate a new clock. A synchronous step can block the main thread's fake-clock advancement while the worker continues running and timestamps a callback timeout. The next request then reports client time more than one second behind that recorded timeout. This condition accepts the regression, allowing subsequent history events—and execution completion—to precede the callback's recorded end. Keep timestamps monotonic within a clock generation and allow backward movement only through an explicit reset signal. Add coverage for a main-thread stall exceeding one second while a worker-side callback timeout fires.
